purpose: The published S-Go claim set (plan §10.1, D76). Every statement here is checked by sgo/scripts/guarantee-check.py against the frozen clauses, SGO_TEST_MATRIX.json and the evidence files. Nothing outside this file is a guarantee.

scope_vocabulary.admission: statically rejected by the compiler, driver or linker
scope_vocabulary.runtime_enforced: checked at run time with a specified failure
scope_vocabulary.model_explored: explored over all interleavings of bounded model scenarios (bounds stated); not a proof for unbounded programs
scope_vocabulary.tested: executed acceptance cases and fixtures only

not_claimed: Proof that an arbitrary S-Go program is correct, terminates, or behaves correctly under all schedules
Compatibility with Go programs or the Go ecosystem
Behavior on targets other than darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64

identity.bootstrap: go1.26.10, recorded by digest in sgo/scripts/fetch-bootstrap.sh

guarantees.statement: A program compiles only if every construct it uses is in the closed S-Go subset (spec 0.10.1): .sgo sources, int/byte/bool/string/error, value structs and arrays, named types with value- and pointer-receiver methods, slices, insertion-ordered maps, pointers, frozen values (sgo.Frozen[T]), function values, the admitted statements. Task-local data (slices, maps, pointers) never crosses tasks except as a deep copy made by sgo.Copy, or frozen by sgo.Freeze, which no task can write (D85, D98–D101). Integer and byte overflow, division by zero, an out-of-range index or slice, a nil dereference, and a write to a nil map are checked failures with a specified record, never wraparound or undefined behavior; map iteration order is insertion order, the same in production and in the lab.

Floating point, anonymous struct types, pointers to handles, range over strings, interfaces, generics, reflection, math/rand, unsafe, cgo, assembly, go:linkname, plugins and raw system calls are rejected at compile time with SGO_E_UNADMITTED; there is no flag, build mode or environment setting that admits them. (Value structs, arrays, and named types are admitted from spec 0.8.0, and slices, maps, and pointers from 0.9.0: G-LANG.)

Variables are task-local; a closure passed to another task may capture only effectively-final variables, so admitted programs have no data races on variables. Communication between tasks happens only through channels, permits, Event and CapacityLimiter, whose operations are synchronizing.

Every task is started in a nursery through its explicit *sgo.Nursery handle and is owned by exactly one nursery; a nursery statement does not complete until all its children have finished (no orphan on any exit, including return, break, panic and cancellation). There is no bare go statement.
guarantees.model_bounds: sgo/model (model.go, explore.go): all interleavings of the 18 W01 scenarios (sgo/evidence/w01/README.md)

guarantees.statement: A child failure cancels its siblings and is reported to the owner; the primary error of a nursery is chosen deterministically (lowest creation id), other errors are chained. A panic unwinds defers and nested nurseries to the task boundary. The process exit status is specified (0 success; 1 an error or child error out of main; 2 any other failure kind such as a panic or checked failure; 3 drain budget exceeded; 4 resource exhaustion or runtime defect), and statuses 1-4 write exactly one diagnostic record.
guarantees.model_bounds: sgo/model (model.go, explore.go): all interleavings of the 18 W01 scenarios (sgo/evidence/w01/README.md)

guarantees.statement: Cancellation is sticky and propagates from a nursery to its descendants; it is observed at the specified checkpoints (blocking operations, sleep, join, Checkpoint). A task that does not cooperate within the drain budget makes the process fail-stop with a diagnostic (exit 3) instead of resuming with the task hidden. Non-cooperative code between checkpoints is not interrupted.
guarantees.model_bounds: sgo/model (model.go, explore.go): all interleavings of the 18 W01 scenarios (sgo/evidence/w01/README.md)
limitations: A task in a loop without checkpoints is detected only by the drain budget, not interrupted (SGO-DRAIN-002).

guarantees.statement: Native channels, select, typed managed channels with send permits, readiness handshakes, Event and CapacityLimiter: each operation has a single commit point; a value is delivered at most once; a reserved permit is committed, aborted, or resolved when its task ends (no capacity leak); a blocked operation of a cancelled task unwinds; a global deadlock is reported, not hung.
guarantees.model_bounds: sgo/model chanmodel/nativemodel: all interleavings of the bounded scenarios, largest 71,549 states (sgo/evidence/w06/README.md, w07/README.md)

guarantees.statement: Effects (clock, wall clock, random, entropy, files, network, simulated store) require a capability that flows from the root grants declared in sgo.mod; a task's authority can only be attenuated, never widened; handles are opaque and cannot be compared or forged; a dependency cannot use an effect its package does not declare.

File access is confined beneath declared directory grants (no '..', absolute-path, prefix or symlink escape, re-verified against concurrent renames); network access is limited to declared TCP endpoints and Unix socket paths. Reads and writes report partial progress; cancelling a shared handle's borrower leaves the owner's handle intact; closed handles are not reused.
guarantees.model_bounds: sgo/model iopath/iohandle: path resolution with renames (14 scenarios) and handle generations (sgo/evidence/w09/README.md)
limitations: Confinement re-verifies the resolved chain; it is not atomic against another process renaming directories concurrently (openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH is not used).

guarantees.statement: A lab build (sgo lab) runs on a deterministic scheduler with virtual time and simulated effects: the same seed and manifest give the same canonical trace, a trace replays exactly, and a divergent or altered trace or a trace of another build is refused. Replay covers managed events (scheduling choices, timers, effect results), not instruction-level replay of arbitrary code. Lab and production artifacts cannot be mixed.
guarantees.model_bounds: sgo/model labmodel: pinned stream goldens and bounded scenarios (sgo/evidence/w08/README.md)

guarantees.statement: Only the trusted files pinned by SHA-256 in TARGET_TCB.json may use unrestricted Go; the driver verifies every trusted Go, assembly and header input before building, and a user package cannot claim a trusted path. Compiled packages carry the spec, admission and TCB identity; stale or foreign objects are refused at import and link. Task stacks are upstream Go's growable stacks (fixed virtual stacks were investigated in W11 and not adopted).

The release is a single-language toolchain: sgo build/run/check/test/fmt/lab plus compile, asm and link, with no go command and no flag, mode or environment variable that reopens stock Go semantics. sgo check and sgo build agree; sgo test runs each test in its own process with its own root nursery and fails tests that leave work behind.

known_limitations.text: Benchmarks report wall, CPU and peak RSS but no allocation counts (T07 PARTIAL, D82).
Fixed-stack experiment cases F03-F05 were not run because no prototype was built (W11 investigated_not_adopted).
No language server; editors get sgo check and sgo fmt only (T03).
